levels.name: First words
levels.sentenceLengthHint: strictly max 6 words per sentence, simple subject-object-verb. The only conjunctions allowed are و and یا joining two nouns or two adjectives (پدر و مادر، خورد و سیاه); never join two clauses, and never use a subordinator (که، چون)
grammarAllowed: present tense mē- verbs (می‌رود, mērawad; می‌خورم, mēkhuram), always spelled with the ZWNJ, and داشتن (to have), whose present is bare دارم/داری/دارد, never a mē- form - both attested throughout the shipped L1 corpus

present tense of budan as the sentence-final copula: ast (است) for 3rd singular, hastam (هستم) for 1st singular - budan's own present is suppletive, so never a mē- form of budan specifically (never می‌است)
strict SOV word order: subject, then object/predicate, then the verb always last - چای خوب است (the tea is good), never خوب است چای

possessive/attributive ezafe links two nouns, or a noun and an adjective, and its script form depends on what the first word ends in: unwritten after a consonant (برادر من, barādar-e man - the vowel is real in speech and simply not spelled) or after silent-he in ordinary Afghan practice (خانه ما, khāna-ye mā - the ZWNJ+ی spelling خانه‌ی is the Iranian convention, not this corpus's), and a plain ی after ا or و (دنیای من, dunyā-ye man)
yes/no questions (rising intonation only, no marker) and chetōr/kujā content questions
negation with نـ (na-) directly on the verb: نیست (nēst) is budan's own suppletive negative, not نه + است

levels.name: Daily life
levels.sentenceLengthHint: strictly max 8 words per sentence, can use simple conjunctions but no complex clauses
grammarAllowed: present tense mē- verbs, always spelled with the ZWNJ (می‌روم, mēravam), never a plain space or fused together (never میروم or می روم); present stems are irregular and must not be guessed from the infinitive

the object marker را marks a definite/specific direct object and is dropped for a generic or indefinite one: من سیب را می‌خورم (I eat the apple - a specific one) but نان می‌خورم (I eat bread - generically) - this is a property of what is meant, not of the noun itself
the indefinite marker ی (yak/-ی) never combines with ezafe on the same noun: یک کتاب or کتابی, never both at once
ham, besyār, negation with na-/namē- (نمی‌روم, nemēravam - same ZWNJ rule as the affirmative)
داشتن (to have) is suppletive like بودن: its present is bare دارم/داری/دارد, never a mē- form - never می‌دارم

levels.name: Short stories
levels.sentenceLengthHint: strictly max 9 words per sentence, may connect with wa/amā/chun
grammarAllowed: simple past and present tenses
future with mē- + context
subordinate clauses with ke
subjunctive (bāyad berawad)
comparatives (-tar)

levels.name: Real texts
grammarAllowed: perfect tenses (rafta ast)
conditional with agar
passive with shudan
relative clauses

levels.name: Culture & ideas
grammarAllowed: reported speech
formal register
idiomatic compounds

levels.name: Near-native
grammarAllowed: unrestricted, including literary forms and poetry excerpts
